description: Solopreneur developer and data analyst building climate/energy data pipelines and forecasting models (wind, solar, hydro) for the Brazilian power grid. Full-stack (Python, FastAPI, React) + AI agents. Looking for a team that ships working prototypes, not pretty slides.
summary:
When a wildfire darkens the sun over Brazil — in drought, in smoke, in sudden solar dips — the grid operator sees only noise. But it was never noise. Hidden inside 42 years of open NASA telemetry (1984–2025), the seasons were always singing their steady song — and the true signal was simply waiting to be heard. Cockpit-OMNI listens.

We built a platform that separates the real trend from the seasonal cycle, turning apparent chaos into a legible story of our climate: which November is normal, and which one is history unfolding. The same sky that feeds Brazil's solar panels is the same sky that will feed the first colonists of Mars — the physics of sunlight knows no borders, and no planets.

That's why this matters. We are not just protecting a power grid. We are proving that the language we learned listening to Earth is the exact language humanity will need when we move to a new world. Cockpit-OMNI is the bridge between the grid that exists and the grid that dreams.
details:
What does it do / How does it work?

Cockpit-OMNI is an open-source analytical platform that ingests 42 years of NASA open telemetry (1984–2025) — solar irradiance (POWER/SRB), atmospheric composition (MERRA-2, OMI), land surface temperature (MODIS), and fire radiative power (FIRMS) — and decomposes every grid cell into three mathematically orthogonal layers:

  1. True Trend — the long-term climate trajectory (warming, drying, aerosol loading)
  2. Seasonal Cycle — the repeating annual rhythm (solstice-driven insolation, monsoon, dry season)
  3. Anomaly / Residual — the event signal: drought onset, wildfire smoke plumes, sudden solar radiation dropouts, extreme heat waves

The engine uses STL (Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LoESS) with adaptive seasonal windows, validated against physical constraints (energy balance, radiative transfer) so the decomposition respects physics, not just statistics. The output is a near-real-time dashboard (Cockpit-OMNI Web) where grid operators, climate scientists, and mission planners can query any coordinate on Earth — and, by parameter swap, any coordinate on Mars — and instantly see: Is this anomaly normal for this season, or is the climate shifting underneath us?

For the power-grid use case (Curve of Duck), the anomaly layer feeds a forecasting pipeline (ARIMA + LightGBM + LSTM ensemble) that predicts the duck-curve neck ramp (evening net-load surge) 6–72 hours ahead, quantifies required storage/hydro reserves, and issues curtailment-risk alerts. The same pipeline, fed with Mars insolation spectra (from MGS/TES, MAVEN, Perseverance MEDA), outputs the Martian duck curve — the sol-by-sol net-load shape a future colony's solar+battery system will face.

https://youtu.be/yqT6piEvZmE

Intended Impact

  1. Operational resilience — Move grid operators from reactive (blackout post-mortem) to anticipatory (dispatch reserves 24 h before the ramp).
  2. Democratized climate intelligence — A favela cooperative in Ceará and a Mars habitat designer in Pasadena open the same notebook, point at their coordinates, and get the same three-layer truth.
  3. Cross-planet knowledge transfer — Prove that the duck-curve problem is universal: wherever sunlight is the primary energy source, the evening ramp exists, and the solution (storage + forecast + reserve market) is structurally identical.
  4. Open science multiplier — All code, data pipelines, and notebooks are MIT-licensed; the 42-year preprocessed cube is published on Hugging Face Datasets for one-line load_dataset() access.How is your project creative?
  5. Physics-constrained STL — Most decompositions are purely statistical. Ours bans trend wiggles that violate surface energy balance (validated against CERES EBAF).
  6. Earth↔Mars parameter swap — One codebase, two planets. The only changes are ephemeris (sol length, obliquity, dust opacity) and insolation spectrum. The duck-curve logic is identical.
  7. Multi-agent autonomous pipeline — 11 specialized agents (ingest → validate → publish) coordinate via a DAG orchestrator written in pure Python asyncio — self-healing, observable, zero external workflow engine.
  8. 42-year cube as a dataset, not a script — Preprocessed, chunked, Zarr-compressed, versioned on HF Hub. Anyone reproduces the decomposition in 3 lines.
  9. Narrative-driven UI — The dashboard doesn't just show charts; it tells the operator: "This November is 2.3σ drier than the 1984–2025 trend. The last time we saw this anomaly pattern, the NE ramp spiked 14 GW in 3 hours."

Factors the team considered

Factor

Decision & Rationale

Data openness

Only NASA/INMET/ONS open data — no proprietary APIs. Reproducible by anyone, anywhere.

Physical interpretability

Rejected black-box transformers; chose STL + physics constraints so every layer has a physical meaning (trend = climate forcing, seasonal = orbital, anomaly = weather/event).

Latency vs. depth

Near-real-time (hourly ingest → 15 min dashboard refresh) for operations; full 42-year recompute monthly for science.

Grid-relevant metrics

Not just MAE/RMSE — Ramp Score, POD/FAR for ramp events, Quantile Loss (P10/P50/P90), LRCAP-equivalent reserve sizing.

Equity of access

PWA works offline on a $100 phone; cube downloadable via wget on 2G; docs in PT/EN/ES.

Mars transferability

Validated Earth pipeline against Mars analogs (Atacama, Devon Island) before claiming cross-planet use.

Governance

MIT license, open governance (CONTRIBUTING.md, RFC process), no vendor lock-in (Supabase is replaceable by Postgres + pgvector).

Team sustainability

Solopreneur core + open contributors; agent orchestration automates 80% of ingest/validate/publish so human effort goes to science, not plumbing.
